get_working_directory.desc: Return the server's current working directory, OS, and hostname. Call this first to orient yourself before navigating the filesystem — most other tools default to 'server's current working directory' and this tells you what that is.

run_command.desc: Execute a shell command and return combined stdout+stderr. Runs via sh -c on Unix, cmd /C on Windows. IMPORTANT: cmd /C does NOT understand Unix shell syntax — `;`, heredocs, single-quoted strings, and `$VAR` expansion do not work; use `powershell -NoProfile -Command "..."` or `bash -c "..."` for Unix-style scripting on Windows. Use max_output_bytes to cap large output and avoid flooding context. detach=true for fire-and-forget processes: returns the PID immediately with no captured output — use list_processes to check status. Timeout default: 60 s, max: 600 s.

params.command: Command string to execute. Chain with && / ; / | as needed. Quote arguments containing spaces.
params.cwd: Working directory. Defaults to server's working directory.
params.timeout_seconds: Seconds before killing the command. Default: 60, max: 600.
params.env: Extra environment variables as ["KEY=value", ...]. Merged with current env.
params.max_output_bytes: Truncate output to this many bytes. Default: no limit.
params.stdin: Content piped to the command's standard input.
params.allow_nonzero_exit: Return non-zero exit codes as success instead of raising an error. Default: false.
params.raw_output: Omit metadata header (command echo, cwd, exit code) — return only stdout/stderr. Use when parsing programmatic output (e.g. JSON). Default: false.
params.detach: Start the process detached (new session via setsid on Unix). Returns immediately with the PID; output is not captured. Use list_processes to monitor. Ignores timeout_seconds, stdin, and max_output_bytes. Default: false.

open_in_app.desc: Open a file, directory, or URL in the default system application. Non-blocking — returns immediately. Uses open on macOS, xdg-open on Linux, start on Windows. Prefer this over running open/xdg-open/start via run_command.

params.target: File path, directory path, or URL to open.

get_env.desc: Read environment variables. With key, returns that variable's exact value. With filter, returns all variables whose name contains the substring (case-insensitive). Without arguments, returns ALL variables — avoid: floods context with 100+ entries and may leak secrets into the conversation. Always prefer key or filter.

params.key: Exact variable name. Returns its value.
params.filter: Case-insensitive substring. Returns all matching KEY=value pairs.
